findings.description: PJE (Psychoemotional Jeopardy Evaluation) appears in prose without glossary coverage. The glossary contains 49 terms but no 'pje' entry. The parenthetical expansion provides local clarity, but readers who encounter PJE elsewhere on the site lack a canonical definition to reference.
findings.suggestion: Add a 'pje' entry to src/data/glossary.ts with category 'framework', definition covering its role as the taxonomy mapping Dreaddit labels to PSQ dimensions, and a 'broader' relationship to 'psq'.
findings.context: remapped through a PJE-derived taxonomy (Psychoemotional Jeopardy Evaluation, a framework this project developed)

findings.description: Specific numerical claim ('improved mean absolute error by 3.5-21.6% per dimension') presented without citation or link to the calibration analysis that produced these figures. Fair witness discipline requires grounding for empirical claims.
findings.suggestion: Add a parenthetical citation or internal link pointing to the calibration analysis source (e.g., a lab-notebook entry or technical appendix) so readers can verify the claimed improvement range.
findings.context: Isotonic regression — a monotonic calibration technique applied post-training — corrected the model's raw outputs toward better alignment with this approximate reference. It improved mean absolute error by 3.5–21.6% per dimension.

findings.description: Claim that recommendation algorithms shape 'billions of information environments' stated as direct observation without sourcing. While the scale claim aligns with widely reported platform user counts (Meta ~3.9B monthly active users across platforms, Google search ~8.5B daily queries), fair witness discipline distinguishes observation from inference. The specific characterization of these as 'information environments' shaped by 'a small clique' carries rhetorical weight that warrants sourcing.
findings.suggestion: Add a parenthetical citation to platform user statistics (e.g., Meta Q4 2025 earnings, Alphabet annual report) to ground the scale claim, or soften to 'billions of users' information environments' with a footnote.
findings.context: Recommendation algorithms at companies like Meta and Google concentrate decision-making power over billions of information environments.

findings.description: Direct quotation attributed to Carter's 1978 Senate transmission message ('The United States can only benefit from a world in which economic and social rights are respected') without a specific citation or link to the document. The OHCHR ICESCR link covers the treaty text, not the transmission message. Historical quotes require traceable sourcing.
findings.suggestion: Add a citation to the Carter transmission message. The American Presidency Project (presidency.ucsb.edu) or the Senate Foreign Relations Committee records may host the text. If the exact source cannot be located, hedge with 'Carter wrote, in substance, that...'
findings.context: Carter's message transmitting the ICESCR to the Senate for advice and consent, sent on February 23, 1978, framed economic rights as consistent with American values.

epistemic_flags: PJE glossary gap (f1) may already have coverage elsewhere on the site that the scan did not check — glossary.ts serves as the canonical source but other pages may define the term inline
Carter quote verification (f4) depends on document availability — the American Presidency Project may or may not host the specific transmission message
